I see - the code frees `node->last` (the last child) when moving up from a node. So it frees the last child of a parent when the reader moves past all children. This means the ID attribute needs to be on a child node that gets freed during reading.

Wait, actually the ID attribute is on the `root` element. The `root` element's children are freed when the reader moves past them. But the ID attribute is on `root` itself, not on its children.

Let me reconsider. The ID attribute is on `root`. When `root`'s children are freed during reading, `xmlTextReaderFreeNode` is called on each child. But the children don't have ID attributes, so `xmlTextReaderRemoveID` is not called.

The ID attribute on `root` would only be freed when `root` itself is freed, which happens in `xmlTextReaderFreeDoc` (via `xmlTextReaderFreeNodeList`). But by that time, the ID table has already been freed.

So the scenario I described earlier (double-free via `xmlTextReaderRemoveID` setting `id->name = attr->name`) doesn't apply because `xmlTextReaderRemoveID` is never called during reading.

Let me think about this differently. What if the double-free happens because of a different mechanism?
